body:
## Summary
Two fixes found while driving the stack from an agent on Windows:

### 1. `browser_navigate` now supports `"back"` / `"forward"` (extension/handlers/navigation.js)
Previously the history keywords were treated as **relative URLs** — `{ url: "back" }` resolved to `chrome-extension://<id>/back`, stranding the tab on a protected page with no way back for the agent.

- `"back"` / `"forward"` now walk the tab history via `chrome.tabs.goBack()` / `chrome.tabs.goForward()`
- The response reports the URL the tab **actually landed on** (not the keyword)
- Tool description updated so agents discover the keywords (`navigate.ts`)

### 2. `scripts/drive.mjs` works on Windows
The helper hard-coded the unix socket `~/.browser-controller/daemon.sock` on every platform; on Windows the daemon listens on the **named pipe** `\\.\pipe\browser-controller` (daemon-config.ts), so it always failed with ENOENT. It now picks the correct transport per platform.

## Test plan
- `npm test` — 275 passing (the daemon IPC suite is environmental-only on Windows while a live daemon owns the fixed named pipe)
- Manual E2E on Windows 11, extension v2.2.x:
  - `browser_navigate { url: "back" }` on a real tab → lands on the previous page, response carries the landed URL
  - `browser_navigate { url: "forward" }` → symmetric
  - `node scripts/drive.mjs` → connects via the named pipe on Windows
- Version bumped to 2.2.1 (manifest + package + README)
